I meditate upon that God whose breath is the wind.
For those abiding in their respective spheres, [he is endowed] with various specific qualities. || 32 ||
I meditate upon that god whom they call the protector of the sense-objects.
He who is beyond time, beyond sacrifice, and beyond both the existent and the non-existent.
I meditate upon that God who is the beginningless origin of the universe.
From whose two feet the earth was born, and likewise from his two ears the quarters of space.

From whose navel [arose] the intermediate space (antarikṣa), and from whose two nostrils the wind (pavana). || 35 ||
I meditate upon that God, from whose perspiration the birth of the waters arises. ||36||
The Lord of Gods, who has the head of a boar, the form of the Man-lion, and the form of the Dwarf.
O Rāma, I am eternally bowed in mind before that Lord of the three worlds, the bestower of boons, the most worthy of praise. ||37||
From his mouth the Brāhmaṇas were produced; from his chest the Kṣatriyas were produced.
From whose pair of thighs the Vaiśyas were likewise born, and from whose feet the Śūdras were produced. ||38||
Likewise, the entire world is pervaded by the manifestations of him who is the source of the existence of all beings.
O Rāma, I bow forever in my mind to that lord of the gods, the giver of boons, the most excellent one. ||39||

Thus ends the fifty-second chapter, titled "The Instruction on the Object of Meditation," within the *Śaṅkaragītā* of the *Śrī-Bhārgava-Rāma-Prashna*, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the first section of the *Śrī-Viṣṇudharmottara*.
Rāma said:
O Maheśvara, [I praise] Varāha, Narasiṃha, and Vāmana.
From you, I wish to hear about the manifestations of the Great-Souled One.

Hiraṇyākṣa, who was difficult to overcome, as well as Hiraṇyakaśipu.

Likewise, while the great asura Hiraṇyākṣa was ruling over Pātāla.

[He saw] the thirty gods who had sought refuge [with him], having been driven out by Hiraṇyākṣa.
Having bound him with the gift of fearlessness, Janārdana released him.

Holding a conch and a discus with his two hands,

Thus ends the fifty-third chapter, titled "The Slaying of Hiraṇyākṣa," within the section on the Manifestation of the Boar, the Śaṅkaragītā, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the first book of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara.
Śaṅkara said:

By means of a radiant celestial chariot, sun-colored and yoked with swans.

By the most meritorious celestial rishis, by the siddhas, and likewise by the seven rishis.
By most meritorious royal sages, by Gandharvas, and by hosts of Apsarases.

Even the sages, O Grandfather of the worlds, could not cast a curse upon me when they were enraged.
"Those endowed with ascetic power might even curse me; this is the boon I choose. (11)
Neither by weapon nor by missile, neither by mountain nor by tree.
My death shall not come by either dry or moist means in any way whatsoever. (12)
May I alone become the sun, the moon, the wind, and the fire.
The waters, the atmosphere, the stars, and the ten directions; || 13 ||
I am anger and desire; I am Varuṇa, Vāsava, and Yama.
And likewise Dhanada, the Yakṣa who is the presiding lord and sovereign of the Kimpuruṣas. || 14 ||
Brahmā said:
"O dear one, these wonderful and excellent divine [weapons] have been given to you by me."
Therefore, you shall obtain all these desires; of this there is no doubt.
Śaṅkara said:

The abode of the gods, Vairāja, frequented by hosts of great sages.
Then the gods, the nāgas, the gandharvas, and likewise the sages [gathered].
Having heard the granting of the boon, they approached the Grandfather.
The gods said:
By means of this boon, that Asura will slay us, O Blessed One.

The Blessed One is the self-existent Lord, the original creator of all beings.

Śaṅkara said:

Then the Giver of Boons spoke these words to all the hosts of gods:

While that excellent one was merely small in size, he oppressed all living beings.
The Daitya Hiraṇyakaśipu was made arrogant by the granting of a boon.

The god Viṣṇu, who consists of Brahman, who is the embodiment of Brahman, and who is eternal.

When the Dānava Hiraṇyakaśipu, that thorn in the side of the gods, was slain.

At that time, he spoke these words in a voice as deep as a thundercloud.

And the highly fortunate sages, whose vision is stainless regarding the three periods of time.
At that very time, however, he was consecrated for the horse sacrifice.
The illustrious Bali, lord of the Daityas, took refuge in Sthaligrāma.
Taking him upon his left shoulder, Bṛhaspati [acted] at that sacrifice of his.
O tiger among the Bhrigus, this was surely brought about by his very power of illusion.
Having reached the sacrificial enclosure, Vāmana praised the sacrifice.
O Brahmin, [he] conceals himself by means of himself, like fire covered by ashes. || 15 ||
And Bali, the best among the upholders of dharma, caused him to enter.
And he beheld the highly fortunate Vāmana, who was exceedingly beautiful.
With all its limbs joined together, it was plump and possessed closely set joints.
He was resplendent with a black antelope skin, matted hair, a staff, and a water-pot. ||17||
About to display his prowess, he contracted like a tiger into his own body.

Thus addressed by the god, Bali, the lord of the hosts of Daityas, [replied].

Moreover, O best of the twice-born, accept whatever else you desire.
And then Hari accepted the water, just as the wind accepts it as it blows.
Like a cloud being gazed upon by the foremost Daityas facing the north.
Let Hari invade the worlds; let the Dānavas take up weapons in their hands.
They charge with speed, possessing various faces and necks.

The Dānavas were terrible, with faces like crocodiles and faces like jackals.

Of lions, tigers, jackals, leopards, monkeys, and birds;

Having obtained the net of offerings, Hari then grew in size.
Like a cloud being gazed upon by hosts of gods facing the north.

They have faces resembling those of fish, turtles, and frogs. || 28 ||

They had tawny eyes, wide-open mouths, and various arms and necks. || 29 ||
They have thick tips on their noses, flat faces, and large jaws and skulls.

Others were adorned with serpent ornaments, and some were decorated with crowns.

Others likewise bore bows and arrows, while others held javelins in their hands.
Others likewise carried swords and shields, while others held iron clubs in their hands. || 32 ||
With *śataghnīs* and discuses in their hands, and maces and clubs in their grasp.

Viṣṇu, the best among the powerful, gave the earth to Śakra.

Bali said:
O God, as much of the earth as has been fashioned by you alone—‖ 43 ‖

Dwell there in the netherworld named Sutala, remaining well-restrained.

You are devoted to Brahman, you are a refuge for others, you are habituated to sacrifice, and you are sweet-spoken.
He was an ascetic, charitable by nature, and one who had mastered the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences.

Śaṅkara said:
Having spoken thus, he, who resembled a water-laden cloud and was clad in garments as bright as refined gold, [proceeded].

Thus ends the fifty-fifth chapter, titled "The Manifestation of Vāmana," in the Śaṅkara-gītās of the Māgha-saṃhitā within the first section of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara.
Rāma said:
Of that Viṣṇu, the god beyond gods, of immeasurable splendor.
From you, I desire to hear of your divine self-manifestations.
Śaṅkara said:
The glories of the God of gods cannot be described in detail.
I shall describe them to you according to their importance; listen with a focused mind, O twice-born one.
Brahmā is in creation, Viṣṇu in preservation, and likewise Hara in dissolution.
Varuṇa, Vāyu, Ākāśa, Jyotis, and likewise Pṛthivī. || 3 ||
And also the cardinal directions, the intermediate directions, as well as those who are the lords of the directions.
The Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Bhṛgus, and likewise the Aṅgirases. || 4 ||

The Aśvins, Puruhūta, and the hosts of Gandharvas and Apsarases. || 5 ||

Whether moving horizontally, upwards, or downwards, or that which does not move at all—its very nature is the Tinge (tviṅgita). || 6 ||
O highly fortunate one, he who is both truth and untruth, as well as nature and its transformation.
Likewise, there are the wombs of worms, insects, moths, and birds.
Likewise, the Vidyādharas, Yakṣas, Nāgas, Sarpas, and Kinnaras.
And the Rākṣasas, the Piśācas, the Pitṛs, and those who are subject to the constraints of time. || 8 ||
Virtue, wealth, desire, and liberation, as well as whatever gateways to virtue there may be.
And all the components of sacrifice, as well as the fourfold collection of living beings. ||9||
Those born from a womb, those born from an egg, those born from moisture, and those born from a sprout.
He is the single light of the Maruts and the Vasus, and he is the Purifier.
And Ahirbudhnya is among the Rudras, while Nāda belongs to the Aśvins.
And Nārāyaṇa was among the Sādhyas, and likewise Kratu was among the Bhṛgus. ||11||
Likewise, Viṣṇu is among the Ādityas, and Āyu is among the Aṅgirases.
And he is celebrated as the one who shines among all the gods. ||12||
Vāsava is the lord of all the gods, and Hutāśana is the lord of the luminaries.
Yama is the lord of those whose nature is self-restraint, and Virūpākṣa is the lord of those who bear patience.
Varuṇa is the lord of aquatic creatures, and likewise, Pavana is the lord of those who move through the air.
Dhanādhyakṣa is the lord of the Yakṣas, and Rudra is likewise the fierce one within.
Ananta is the foremost among all nāgas, and the sun is likewise the foremost among radiant beings.
Likewise, among the planets the Moon is foremost, and among the constellations, Kṛttikā.
Time is the best among those things that calculate, and the Kṛta Yuga is the best among the ages.
The lords of the manvantaras and the fourteen Manus endure for one kalpa.
He alone is the god who is the self of all, as well as those who are the lords of the gods.
The year, as well as the rains and the northern course [of the sun], are likewise [to be known]. || 17 ||
Among the months, Mārgaśīrṣa is indeed the spring among the seasons.

The killing of the *kāraṇas* has been declared, as well as that of the *muhūrtas*, including Abhijit.
Among the netherworlds, Sutala is the foremost; among the oceans, the Ocean of Milk is the foremost. || 19 ||
And among the continents, Jambūdvīpa is said to be the truth of worlds.

I shall invoke Ṛkṣa and Āśvinī, who grant all desires.
The invocation of Yama has been declared; now listen to that which pertains to Bharaṇī.
I shall invoke the fierce constellation named Bharaṇī.
Come, O Goddess Bharaṇī, fortunate one of lovely appearance!
O King, the invocation of Śakra has already been described by me previously.
I shall invoke the eastern direction, adorned by the rising sun.
Come, O bestower of boons, you who formerly accomplished auspicious deeds! || 101 ||
The invocation of the Fire-god has already been explained by me to you previously.
I shall invoke the quarter that bestows boons, situated between the east and the south.
O beloved of Agni, O bestower of boons, come hither from the southeast.
The invocation of Yama has been declared; now hear [the procedure] for the southern direction.
I shall invoke [the deity] from the southern direction, the most excellent southern quarter.
O auspicious one, you should proceed to the south in all ritual activities. || 104 ||
The invocation of the wise Virūpākṣa has been described previously.
I shall invoke the auspicious direction, the south-west.
Come to me, O Goddess Nairṛtī, who constantly increases prosperity!
I have thus declared the invocation of the high-souled Varuṇa.
I shall invoke the auspicious western quarter, belonging to Varuṇa.
Come, O Goddess, in the west, O bestower of boons, beloved of Varuṇa! || 107 ||
I have thus declared the invocation of the high-souled Vāyu.
I invoke Vidisha, situated in the northwestern direction between the west and the north.
O Giver of Boons, come toward me from the northwest.
I invoke the god Dhanada, the lord Vaiśravaṇa.
O King of Kings, O Lord of the wealth of all sacrifices, come hither!
I shall invoke the northern quarter, which is protected by the Giver of Wealth.
O beautiful one, you should proceed with all the rites hereafter.
The invocation of the great-souled Tryambaka, the god, has thus been declared. || 111 ||
I shall invoke the auspicious northeastern direction.
"Come, O blessed goddess, who are ever protected by Śiva! (112)
I shall invoke all the oceans into the eastern jars.
"Let the four ocean-guardians of jewels come here. || 113 ||
In the northeastern direction, the ocean belongs to that which is the eastern jar.
May the auspicious Dakṣiṇa come from the southeast, and may the southern one arrive in the south. || 114 ||
But let the western [deity] come together with the southern-western one in the water-pot.
And let Uttara likewise enter the pitcher in the north-western direction.
Once they have been invoked, one should perform the rite after placing the head [of the vessel] upon the ground.
Having performed a prostration and offered salutation, one should then recite the mantra.
Indeed, it is through your favor and by means of our worship of you.
I shall strive according to my ability; you ought to grant me permission for this. || 117 ||
By whom is it possible to perform your worship according to the prescribed rule?
How can the great state be attained by one who is devoid of worship of you? || 118 ||
Therefore, I shall perform a return-honor for you according to my ability.
O givers of boons, I shall strive [to do so]; therefore, you should grant me permission for that.
In this ritual of worship to you, there are indeed always many who are highly learned.
The guardians of the quarters, blazing with splendor, each took their respective position in their own direction.
May they destroy all the obstacles that have arisen for me.
May the Brahma-rākṣasas, who destroy sacrifices, perish from this land! || 121 ||
The fierce Vināyakas who create obstacles, those who hate the sacrifice, and those who devour flesh;

Having said this much, the wise man should scatter white mustard seeds in the cardinal and intermediate directions.
And likewise, the mantra "rakṣohaṇam" should be recited aloud here by the eminent twice-born.
O one of undaunted spirit, for the worship of all the grahas, bathing with all medicinal herbs has been prescribed.
Likewise with all seeds, as well as with perfumes, earths, jewels, and waters. || 124 ||

Thus ends the ninety-fifth chapter, titled "The Chapter on the Mantras for Invoking the Planets and Constellations," in the first section of the Śrī Viṣṇudharmottara, within the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra. || 95 ||

But tell me of the perfumes and garlands for all of them as well.

And of the gods established in their fixed abodes, O lord of the earth.

Jātī and lavaṅga, well-ground, should be offered to Vāsava.
And likewise, camphor for Vāruṇa, and for Ājā and Ahirbudhnya.
Red sandalwood is for Pūṣan, and likewise white [sandalwood] is for the Aśvins.
Likewise, that which originates from the deer should be given together with aguru in the southern direction.
The deity and the lunar mansion are likewise said to be common to all directions.

It is auspicious, it is purifying, and it is beloved by the gods.

O foremost of kings, whatever has been stated by me regarding this planet or this constellation—

Thus ends the ninety-sixth chapter, titled "The Description of Ointments," in the first section of the Śrī Viṣṇudharmottara, within the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
O Lord of the World, the planets, the lunar mansions, and the directions are of the same color.
One who understands should constantly give garments and banners. || 1 ||
And auspicious golden ornaments should also be given.
O lord of men, [he gave] delightful objects variegated with jewels according to his ability. || 2 ||
O lord of the earth, [this concerns] the deities who are established in their fixed abodes.
Jāti flowers should be offered to all without distinction.
Red lotuses are for the Sun, and white lotuses are for the Moon.
And bandhūka flowers for Bhauma, and blue lotuses for Budha. || 4 ||
Yellow jasmine is for the yellow [deity], and likewise white jasmine is for the white [deity].
Bāṇa flowers for Saura, and Pāṭala flowers for Rāhu. || 5 ||
Likewise, O lord of the earth, the *damanaka* flower should be given to the *ketu*.
And under the asterism Kṛttikā, O King, red lotuses should be offered.

Nevertheless, for this Vaiśvadeva sacrifice, there are white lotuses as well as the kubjaka flower.
For the Brahma-mantra, jasmine flowers; for the Vaiṣṇava-mantra, the campaka flower.
The *pāṭalā* belongs to Vāsava, while the blue lotuses belong to Varuṇa.
Furthermore, O King, his *arka* flowers should likewise be offered.
And the flowers of the Dhattūra should be offered to Āhirbudhnya.
Likewise, O King, there are karavīraka flowers under the asterism of Pauṣṇa.

Likewise, those [omens] declared for the directions based on the common constellation of one's birth.

Whatever secret has been spoken by me here, O preeminent lord of the earth, regarding the bear—

Thus ends the ninety-seventh chapter, titled "The Chapter on Flowers to be Offered and Those Not to be Offered According to Specific Planets and Constellations," in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra within the first section of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara. 97.

Curd-water, as well as celvala seeds and the flesh of deer;

With waters of Varuṇa, as well as with flowers and auspicious unbroken grains (akṣata).

O foremost of kings, whatever has been stated by me here regarding the planets or the lunar mansions—
In the same manner, offerings should likewise be given to the deity of that [direction] and to the directions themselves; there is no doubt in this matter. || 19 ||
Thus ends the one hundred and first chapter, titled "The Classification of Materials for the Homa," in the first section of the Śrī Viṣṇudharmottara, within the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
An oblation for Dhruva should be performed with the mantra beginning "dhruvā dyauḥ."
"Upward" and "downward"—thus [the directions] of the fixed quarter (the zenith) and [the nadir] come to be. || 1 ||
"This is proclaimed as the Brahma-yajña of Brahman."

Kāvākṣi, Puṣpadh, and Kṣīrakāraṇḍi.
Kṣapādi, Kareri, Pārikā, and Īri as well.
Thus have all the ancestral lineages (pravara) of the Ṛṣis been proclaimed.
And likewise Āṅgiras, Utathya, and the sage Dīrghatapas.
These are proclaimed to be mutually ineligible for intermarriage. || 12 ||
Uṣṭa, Ajiṣṭa, Ayasya, Kakṣīvat, and likewise Gotama.
Listen now to their ancestral lineages and their respective *pravara* groups. || 13 ||
And Aṅgiras, and Tatas, and the great ṛṣi Uṣājis;
Saumastambhi, Vitambhi, Sālubhi, and likewise Vālubhi; || 14 ||
Bhāradvāji, Saubuddhi, Meghī, and likewise Devamati.
Ādryāyaṇa and Sāviṣṭya were the sons of Agniveśa Śalāthali. || 15 ||
Vāliśeyī, Niśśaikayī, Vārāhī, and likewise Vākali.
Śāṭi, Ṛṣivarṇa, Prāvāhi, and Āśvalāyani;
The sages are proclaimed to be mutually ineligible for intermarriage. || 16 ||
Kāvāki, Sabhākāyi, and likewise the lord Aṃśumati.
Bhāvīka, Eyūrinai, Bhulvi, and likewise Puṣpānveṣin. ||17||
Bādhyo, Vicchindiśāṭīki, and likewise Khāragrīvi.
Devādyāri, Devasthāni, Harikarṇi, and Sabhrāṅgika; || 18 ||
Dhaivāyi, Sābhimukhi, and likewise Gomadagandhika.
Mātsyakvātha, Sālahara, Hyaloha, and likewise Hāra. || 19 ||
Gāgodayi, Kautapati, and likewise Kaurukṣetri.
Tāṭākī, Jaiñyadroṇī, and Jaivālāyani; ||1.112.20||
Āpa, Tadharmaja, Dṛṣṭi, and Kārṣṇapiṅgali;
And also the highly resplendent Paulas and Śaṅkalāyani. || 21 ||
O King, the ancestral lineage (pravara) of all these [sages] is according to their seer-names (ārṣeya).
Aṅgiras is their first pravara, and Bṛhaspati is the second. || 22 ||
And Bharadvāja is the third; these are proclaimed as the Pravaras.
These are proclaimed to be mutually ineligible for intermarriage. || 23 ||
The Kāṇāyanas, the Kaupayavas, and likewise the Vātsyaparāyaṇas.
Bhrāṣṭrakṛt, Bhrāṣṭravindī, Nendrāli, and Sayakāyana. ||24||
Kroḍi, Śākrī, Kārṣī, Tālakṛt, and Māthurāvatā.
The monkey Pailukāyana was one who caused the Brahmin Bhāla to be led away. || 25 ||
Likewise Mṛtsaṃśa, Akrī, Garga, and Śyāmāyani.
Vālali and Sāhari are likewise proclaimed as having five ancestral seers (pañcārṣeya). || 26 ||
But Aṅgiras, the preceptor of the gods, Bṛhaspati, was possessed of great splendor.
Bharadvāja, as well as Garga and the venerable seer Caitya. || 27 ||
The sages are proclaimed to be ineligible for intermarriage with one another.
Kapītara, Svastitara, Darbha, Śakti, and Patañjali. || 28 ||
Furthermore, there were Jalasandhi, Bindudaṇḍin, and Kuśītakin.
Bhṛgu, Rājakeśī, Śaumbāṭi, and likewise Śāṃśibi; || 29 ||
Śāli, Śakala Kāṇva, and likewise the sage Kerīrayi.
Kādyo, Vādhyāyani, and Sāvasyāyani. || 1.112.30 ||
O best of kings, their lineage is that of Tyārṣeya, and this is their ancestral succession by name.
Aṅgiras, Amavāhya, and likewise Atatkṣaya; || 31 ||
All of them are declared to be ineligible for intermarriage with one another.
Sakṛti, Trimārṣṭi, Śedhū, and Śaipavir as well. || 32 ||
Taṇḍi, Jānaki, and Tailakādravya as well.
Nārāyaṇi, Ārṣabhi, Laukṣi, Gārgi, and likewise Hala. || 33 ||
Gālava also has three ancestral seers (tryārṣeya); these are considered the pravaras for all [of them].
Aṅgiras, Saṃkṛti, and likewise Gaurivīti. ||34||
O sages, they have been declared to be mutually ineligible for intermarriage.
Kāṇvāyana, Haritaka, Kautsya, and likewise Pauṅgya. || 35 ||
Hastidama, Vātsyamālin, Māndri, Gāli, and Gaveraṇa.
Those of the Bhīmaveśa lineage are considered to have Śaṅkha as their ancestor; all these possess three pravaras. || 36 ||
Aṅgiras, as well as Tamasū, Purukutsa, and likewise [others].
The Kutsas are not to be married with the Kutsas; thus say the ancients.
The Rathītaras are proclaimed as the most eminent, having three ancestral sages (tryārṣeya).
Aṅgiras, Surūpa, and likewise Rathītara. || 38 ||
Those who are not charioteers should not marry women who are charioteers, nor should those who are charioteers marry women who are not charioteers.
Viṣṇuvṛddhi, Śaga, Madri, Jatriṇa, and likewise Kartriṇa. || 39 ||
And Praḍivah, possessed of great splendor, as well as Parāyaṇa.
And for all of them, the auspicious *pravara* consisting of three *ṛṣis* is considered the standard.
Aṅgiras, Virūpa, and likewise Pṛthudaśva.
These are proclaimed to be mutually ineligible for marriage. || 41 ||
Śānti, Amugdhi, Mahātejas, Hiraṇyastambin, and Mudgala.
O King, even among all these, the Pravara consisting of three Ṛṣis is considered their [standard] one.
Aṅgiras, Gṛtsamada, and Mudgala of great asceticism.
These are proclaimed to be mutually ineligible for marriage. || 43 ||
Mohajihva, Devajihva, Agnijihva, and Virāḍa;
These two, Apāneya and Tryagra, were the descendants of Audgala through Vairiṇī. || 44 ||
Even for those who have three ṛṣis, this auspicious pravara is considered valid for all of them.
Aṅgiras, Tāviśa, and Maudgalya of great asceticism. || 45 ||
The sages are declared to be ineligible for intermarriage with one another.
Uruṇḍa, Bhuruṇḍa, and the third, Śākaṭāyana. || 46 ||
Then, in order of increasing inferiority: a woman, a monkey, a lover, and hemp.
And likewise the Kāṇvas and Mārkaṭas, as well as the sage Rāmavaṇa, by her [were begotten]. || 47 ||
Likewise, for these Śyāmāyanas, the pravara is considered to be three-ṛṣi.
Aṅgiras, Ajamīḍha, and Kaṇva of great asceticism; || 46 ||
The sages are proclaimed to be ineligible for intermarriage with one another.
Tittiri, Kapibhu, and the great ṛṣi Gārgya; || 49 ||
The sages are proclaimed to be ineligible for intermarriage with one another.
The auspicious ancestral lineage (pravara) of all these [sages] by name is that of the seers (ārṣeya).
Aṅgiras, Tittiri, and the great ṛṣi Kapibhū.
The sages are proclaimed to be ineligible for intermarriage with one another.
Aṅgiras, along with Bharadvāja, the Ṛṣi Vandin, and likewise Navas; || 52 ||
Bṛhaspati, and Maitravacas—these are proclaimed as the five ancestral seers (pañcārṣeya).
Aṅgiras, along with Bharadvāja, and likewise Bṛhaspati. || 53 ||
The seer Ṛṣimitravacas and the seer Vāndatavas likewise.
The sages are proclaimed to be mutually ineligible for intermarriage.
Bhāradvāja, Kaṭa, Auśija, and likewise Śaithireya.
Thus all these have been described as those born of two fathers (dvyāmuṣyāyaṇas). ||55||
Thus, although these [lineages] have five fire-origins (pañcāgneya), their pravaras are proclaimed as follows.
Aṅgiras together with Bharadvāja, and likewise Bṛhaspati; || 56 ||
The Sauṅgas and the Śaiśavis are likewise proclaimed as the most eminent lineages.
The sages are proclaimed to be ineligible for intermarriage with one another. ||57||
These, O King, have been described to you as the high-souled founders of lineages in the family of Aṅgiras.
And by the recitation of whose names a person abandons all evil entirely. || 58 ||

Thus ends the one hundred and twelfth chapter, titled "The Description of the Genealogy of Aṅgiras," in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra within the first section of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Learn from me about those born in the lineage of Atri who were the founders of lineages.
The Karpūrāyaṇas, the Śākheyas, and those who are the Śārāhaṇas;
Śaivālakī, Śaunavarṇi, and those who were swift in their deeds, such as Aghosa; || 1 ||
The Gauragrīvas, the Kārañjas, and those who are the Maitrāyaṇas.
The Ātmanya, Vāmarathya, Gaupāyana, Āstākī, and Bindu [are the teachers]. ||2||
Hvānajitbāhu, Indra, Viraindra, Āli, and Śākaṭāyana.
Taileya, Bauleya, and likewise the Atrigauṇī intellect. || 3 ||
Jalada, Bhagapāda, Sopuṣpi, and Mahātapas;
Likewise, among these, the Chāndogya is considered their ancestral lineage (ārṣeya) and pravara. ||4||
Dhyāraśva, likewise Atri, and Ṛcanānas as well.
The sages are proclaimed to be ineligible for intermarriage with one another. ||5||
Dakṣibali, Pālakṛt, Aurṇanābhi, Sili, and Mili.
Bījavāpin, Śirīṣa, Mauñjakeśa, and Gaviṣṭhira. ||6||
Likewise, for these [Baladhana and others], the Pravara is considered to be Tryārṣeya.
Atri, Gaviṣṭhira, and likewise Pūrvātithi are recorded as such;
these sages are proclaimed to be ineligible for intermarriage with one another.
Henceforth, learn from me concerning the Ātreyas and the sons of appointed daughters (putrikā-putras).
Hāleya, Savāleya, and likewise Vāmamathya.
The Gotreyas and the Gotreyās are proclaimed to be those who have three ancestral seers (tryārṣeya). || 9 ||
Atri, Vāmarathya, and the great ṛṣi Potri;
The sages are proclaimed to be ineligible for intermarriage with one another.
Thus, O King, those of great power who were the founders of lineages born from the Ikṣvāku dynasty have been described to you.
But by the recitation of whose names a person abandons all evil entirely. || 11 ||

Thus ends the one hundred and thirteenth chapter, titled "The Genealogy of the Lineage of Atri," in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra within the first section of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
O King, I shall now describe to you another lineage of Atri.
The illustrious Soma was born from Atri; the king was born from his lineage. || 1 ||
But Viśvāmitra attained the status of a Brahmin through ascetic penance.
I shall proclaim his lineage; listen to me as I speak it.
Viśvāmitra, Devarāta, as well as Cekitāna and Gālava.
Vataṇḍa, Śalaṅga, and likewise Aśvatāyana. || 3 ||
Śyāmāyana, Yājñavalkya, Jābāli, and Saindhānāyana.
The Dābhravyas, the Kārīṣīs, the Sauśrutyas, and the Sauśrutās. || 4 ||
The Aulūṣas, the Aupagavayas, and the Pāṇyodarayamāñcayas.
The Kharabādhās, Bahalayas, Pāṇatambas, and Sakauśikas. || 5 ||
The three ancestral sages (trārṣeya) are proclaimed as the lineage-seers (pravara) for all of them.
Viśvāmitra, Devarāta, and Uddāla are great yakṣas.
The sages are declared to be ineligible for intermarriage with one another.
Likewise, Mārgamitra, Ādya, and Mādhucchandasa; || 7 ||
These sages are proclaimed as the three ancestral seers (trārṣeya) of the pravara lineages.
Viśvāmitra was likewise the eldest, as was Madhucchandas. || 8 ||
The sages are proclaimed to be ineligible for intermarriage with one another.
Dhanañjaya, Kapardeya, and Parikuṣṭa, O King.
And Pāṇini; all these are proclaimed as having three ancestral seers (tryārṣeya).
Viśvāmitra, Madhucchandas, and likewise Aghamarṣaṇa.
The sages are declared to be ineligible for intermarriage with one another.
The Kāmalāyanijas and likewise the Āśmarathyas. || 11 ||
And the Bandhulis, who have three ancestral sages (tryārṣeya), are considered the pravaras for all [these groups].
Viśvāmitra, Aśmaratha, and Badhūli of great asceticism; || 12 ||
The sages are proclaimed to be ineligible for intermarriage with one another.
The Pūraṇas, who run about, are proclaimed to have two ancestral sages (dvyārṣeya). || 13 ||
Viśvāmitra and Pūraṇa are remembered as their two pravaras.
The Parivartas and Pūraṇas are not to intermarry with one another. || 14 ||
The Lohitas and Aṣṭakas are likewise proclaimed to have three ancestral seers (tryārṣeya).
Viśvāmitra, Lohita, and Aṣṭaka of great asceticism. || 15 ||
The Aṣṭakas are always characterized by redness; those who are not eligible for marriage should not intermarry with one another.
Udarendra, Kanyaka, the sage Codāvahi, and likewise [the others]. ||16||
And for all of them, even one who has three ṛṣis as his ancestors is considered to have an auspicious lineage.
Ṛṇavān, Grathita, and likewise Viśvāmitra. || 17 ||
The sages are proclaimed to be ineligible for intermarriage with one another.
Audumbari, Śaiśiriṭi, and likewise Ṛṣi Tārkṣyāyaṇa. || 18 ||
Ṭaikāyani, Ṭaikāyani, Tārkṣāyaṇi, and Atharvaṇa.
Kātyāyanī, Karīrāmī, Śālaṅkāyanī, and Lāvakī. 19.
And the venerable Mauñjāyani; these are proclaimed as the three ancestral seers (ṛṣis).
Kili, Kali, as well as the learned Viśvāmitra, and likewise [the others].
The sages are proclaimed to be ineligible for intermarriage with one another.
O lord of men, these highly exalted Kuśikas, the foremost among the twice-born, have been described to you.
But by the recitation of whose names a person abandons all evil entirely. || 21 ||
Thus ends the one hundred and fourteenth chapter, titled "The Genealogy of Viśvāmitra," in the first section of the Śrī Viṣṇudharmottara, within the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Kaśyapa was the son of Marīci, and likewise in the lineage of Kaśyapa.
I shall describe the sages who established the lineages; hear their names from me.
The Āgrāyaṇas, the Jhaṣagaṇas, and the Meṣakaurīṭikāyanas.
Guruvraja, Māṭhara, Gojāviratha, and Lakṣmaṇa. || 2 ||
The Śālāhaleyas, the Kaurijyas, the Aukanyas, and the Āsurāyaṇas.
The slow-moving ones, seeking the waters, go toward the roaring currents. 3.
Those who travel by way of the gods, those who travel by way of the cows, and those who rise upward;
They possess swift horses, variegated steeds, and are equipped with yokes and maces.
Kātuvandin, Mahācakra, and likewise Dākṣapāṇi;
The Grīvāyanas, the Harkiras, and likewise the Hāstidāsas; || 5 ||
The Vātsyas, the Vālinyakṛtas, the Hāsas, the Tālāyanis, and the Sāsas.
Āgrāyaṇa, Pelumūlin, and likewise Rāśvatātaya for us.
The Kauśītakas, the Pākāntas, and those who are the Agniśarmāyaṇas.
The Maiṣeyas, the Kaivameyas, and likewise the Subabhravas. ||7||
The eastern path is indeed the gateway to knowledge and the foremost means of attainment.
The Śyāmocarās, the Naimiṣeyas, and those who dwell there, the Śādvalāyanas. ||8||
The women named Kāṣṭhahāyana and Rīcā, as well as the Ḍaujihāyanas and the Hāstikas.
The Vaikarṇeyas, the Kāśyapas, the Śāmiśās, and the Hāritāyanas. ||9||
The Mātaṅginas and Babhrusavas are proclaimed to have three ancestral seers (tryārṣeya).
Vatsara, Kaśyapa, and Nidhruva of great asceticism; || 1.115.10 ||
The sages mentioned previously are declared to be ineligible for intermarriage with one another.
The Raihās and the Sāṃkhyamitras are proclaimed as the Ṛṣi-lineages.
Vatsāra, Kaśyapa, and Raibhya of great asceticism.
Two lineages are proclaimed to be mutually ineligible for marriage. || 12 ||
Henceforth, I shall indeed proclaim those born of the lineage of Āmuṣyāyaṇa.
The Ānuṣṭubh meters are the branches of the Bhāktara; they are the self-dependent royal lineages. || 13 ||
Śairiśira, Devahi, Sairandhrī, Raupāsī, and Vaki.
Sāluli, Kāṭuvigākṣi, and likewise Śataśambhi; || 14 ||
These Vasiṣṭhas are to be known as [the protectors] by day, and the Kāśyapas by night.
And likewise, all of them have auspicious lineages (pravara) consisting of three ṛṣis.
Vatsāra, Kaśyapa, and Vasiṣṭha of great asceticism;
The sages are proclaimed to be ineligible for intermarriage with one another. || 16 ||
She was Mātā, Baliputra, Bhaupyala, and Jalatvara.
Muñjāmayūra, Paryaśca, and the eighth is Gardabhīmukha. || 17 ||
Hiraṇyabāhu, Kairāta, and both Kāśyapa and Gobhila.
Āhala, Vṛṣakaṇḍa, Sṛketu, and likewise Uttara; || 18 ||
The Udakebhastṛṇas, the Vatsyas, and those who are the Mahākeralas.
Śāḍīlava, Vaiśānava, Sau, Drāvol, Eva, Layāta, and Vaḥ. ||19||
Paippalādi, Pūrvavari, Vīravitti, and Varīnika.
And for all of them, even one who has three ṛṣis as his ancestors is considered to have an auspicious lineage.
Asita Devala, and Kaśyapa of great asceticism;
The sages are proclaimed to be ineligible for intermarriage with one another.
But from Kaśyapa, the foremost of sages, through the daughters of Dakṣa, all [beings] were produced.
O chief of the Yadu-siṃhas, I shall describe that entire world to you later on.
Thus ends the one hundred and fifteenth chapter, titled "The Genealogy of Kaśyapa's Lineage," in the first section of the Śrī Viṣṇudharmottara, within the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Learn from me as I speak of the Brahmins born in the lineage of Vasiṣṭha.
And the lineage (pravara) of the Vasiṣṭhas is proclaimed to consist of a single ṛṣi. || 1 ||
The Vāsiṣṭhas are indeed the descendants of Vasiṣṭha; they are not to intermarry with those born of Vasiṣṭha.
The Vyāghrapādas, the Aupagavas, the Vaiklavas, and the Śādvalāyanas. || 2 ||
The Kāpiṣṭhalas, Kṣaitalomas, Āśvalas, and Sarvaṭākaras.
The two kalpas, Gopāyana and Bodhaya, were created as outsiders.
Bāliśeya, Pāliśiṣya, as well as Umāṅkura and those others.
The Āyasthūṇas, the Śītavṛkṣas, and likewise the Brahmapurohitas. || 4 ||
Lomātya, Svastikara, Māṇḍali, and Gautali;
Vāhni, Haṇḍi, Sumanas, Śvapādi, and Viddhi. || 5 ||
Śauli, Lolir, Brahmabala, and Vailiśravasa as well.
Mauṇḍava and Yājñavalkya, O King, likewise have a single ṛṣi as their lineage ancestor.
Vasiṣṭha is the foremost among these; they are not to intermarry with one another.
Śailālaya, Mahākarṇa, Kauravya, and likewise Kraivaṇi. ||7||
The kapiñjala, the young peacock, and those who are devoted to the path of Viṣṇu;
The Kaurāyaṇas, Lākahayas, and Kaulakṛdbhāgurāyaṇas. || 8 ||
Those who offer vegetables as their oblation, those who drink from the skin of a lizard, and likewise those who drink from the amnion;
The Sāṅkhyāyanas [use] an ox, and likewise the Māṣaśirādhayas. || 9 ||
The Dāmakāyana, the Vāhayava, and likewise the Vākyayoga-ratha.
And the Ābāyana sages, and those who are the Kroḍādānavas.
And the sages Pralambāyana and Aupamanyava as well.
And the Sāṅkhyāyana sages, as well as those who are Daśerakas. || 11 ||
The Pādakāyanas, the Audgrāhas, the Ṛṣis, and the Lekhayas.
Māleya, Brahmavalaya, and likewise Pūrṇāgāri; || 12 ||
And for all of these, the three-sage lineage (tryārṣeya) is likewise considered their pravara.
Bhaga, Vasu, Vasiṣṭha, and Indra, as well as Sammati; || 13 ||
The sages are proclaimed to be ineligible for intermarriage with one another.
The Aupasvasthas, the Svasthalayas, the Vālas, the Hālas, and those who are the Hayas.
The Madhyandinā, Akṣatayaḥ, Paippalā, and Devicaṅkapī.
The Traiśṛṅgas, Vanagas, Ālavas, and Kuṇḍinas, O best of men. (19)
Even for those who have three ṛṣis as their ancestors, this auspicious pravara is considered valid for all of them.
Vasiṣṭha, Mitra, Varuṇa, and Kuṇḍina of great asceticism. || 16 ||
The sages are proclaimed to be ineligible for intermarriage with one another.
Jātūkarṇas, Yavas, and likewise Pādapas; || 17 ||
And for all of them, the *pravara* is likewise considered to be three *ṛṣis*.
Jātūkarṇa, Vasiṣṭha, and likewise Antya, O King.
The sages are proclaimed to be ineligible for intermarriage with one another. || 18 ||
O King, these foremost sages, the founders of lineages, have been described by me as belonging to the family of Vasiṣṭha.
But by the recitation of whose names a person abandons all evil entirely. ||19||
Thus ends the one hundred and sixteenth chapter, titled "The Genealogy of the Lineage of Vasiṣṭha," in the first section of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara Purāṇa. 116.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
But Vasiṣṭha, possessed of great splendor, was formerly the family priest of Nimi.
O best of kings, there were sacrifices performed by him on all sides.
O best of kings, with a tranquil soul, he then rested there in ancient times.
Having gone there, Nimi, the best of kings, spoke these words.
"O Blessed One, I desire to perform a sacrifice; therefore, please officiate for me without delay."
The immensely radiant Vasiṣṭha spoke to that best of kings.
Wait for some time until your sacrifices have been completed on all sides.
"I am exceedingly weary; having rested, O King, I shall perform the sacrifice for you."
Thus addressed, that best of kings replied to Vasiṣṭha.
In matters concerning the next world, who would venture to wait?
O Brahmin, he for whom there is no friendship with the all-powerful Kṛtānta [Death].
One must act with haste in performing the work of the Dharma, for life is indeed fleeting.
A living being who delights in the path of Dharma enjoys happiness even after death. || 7 ||
One should do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's task in the forenoon.
For death does not wait to see whether one's work is finished or not.
One who is attached to fields, offspring, and home, with his mind directed elsewhere—
Like a she-wolf seizing a lamb, death comes and carries one away.
Time has no one who is dear to it, nor does it have anyone who is hateful.
When the karma pertaining to lifespan is exhausted, it forcibly carries away the person.
The vital breath is indeed wind, and that wind possesses the quality of motion is already well known.
O Brahmin, that life which is lived there for even a mere moment is truly wonderful.
Thus, having gathered the necessary provisions, I have come to your feet.
If you do not officiate as my priest, I shall go to another sacrificer.
Thus addressed at that time by Nimi, that best of Brahmins—
Out of anger, he cursed that Nimi, saying, "You shall become bodiless."
Since you have abandoned me, who am exhausted, for another excellent brahmin, [you shall suffer].
Being a knower of dharma, O lord of men, you ought today to appoint a priest.
Then he replied to Nimi, who was devoted to the performance of righteous deeds:
"You create obstacles for no other reason than that you desire to officiate as a priest yourself."
Therefore, I pronounce this curse upon you: today you shall become bodiless.
When this had been said, those two—the brahmin and the king—became bodiless.
The two souls of those [deities], being devoid of bodies, approached Brahmā.
Then, when the two had arrived nearby, Brahmā spoke these words.
"From this day forward, O Nimi, I grant you life and your own place."

"I shall not kill you for your sake, O knower of dharma; let your fear depart."
You are devoted to me, and likewise, I am devoted to my devotees.
"O illustrious one, there is nothing that cannot be given; therefore, go forth at ease."
Having taken up those Daityas who remained after the slaughter and had resorted to the path of the virtuous.
Having spoken thus to Prahrāda, she vanished right there.
O lion among kings, this account of the deeds of Vārāha, which destroys all impurities, has been told by me to you.
Of him who subdues the arrogant Daityas, who is praised by the sages, and who struck down the foremost of the Asuras while scratching his itch; || 31 ||

Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-sixth chapter, titled "The Manifestation of Varāha in Pātāla," in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra within the first section of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara.
Vajra said:
And, O best of the twice-born, hear what Diti did when her sons were destroyed.
Tell me that in brief, for I have a great doubt regarding it.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
And Diti, O King, having lost her sons, practiced great asceticism.
Then she propitiated her husband, the sage Kaśyapa.
Having been propitiated by her excellent asceticism, he invited the beautiful woman to choose a boon.
And at the proper time, with a boon, he [comforted] her who was emaciated by the calamity of her son's death.
Kaśyapa said:
Choose a boon, O lady of beautiful hips; I have arrived as the granter of boons.
Thus addressed, the goddess, deprived of her son, chose a boon.
Diti said:
O Brahmin, I desire a glorious son who shall be the slayer of Śakra.
If you are pleased with me, O Brahman, grant that son back to me.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Thus addressed, her husband, not being very pleased, then spoke these words: "Choose a boon."
Thus it shall come to pass for you, O blessed lady, if you remain pure.
And for a full thousand years it shall be so, and not otherwise.
Having spoken thus, the twice-born dwelt with her for that night.
Then that righteous-souled one, firm in his resolve, departed for the sake of ascetic penance.
Then the goddess Diti, while pregnant, undertook a vow of religious observance.
But seeing her established in her religious observances, Śakra spoke these words: ||| 8 ||
Śakra said:
"O Queen, I shall always perform service for you."
Since I am established in this formidable vow, you ought to grant me permission for it.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Then the god Purandara was addressed by her with the words, "So be it."
He lived there, seeking an opportunity for deception, while always attending to his mother.
Then, O King, when the remainder of her year had passed, Aditi slept during the day.
At the time of midday, O King, she placed her head at his feet.
Having found that opening of hers, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the conqueror of enemy cities, [attacked].
He entered through the opened path of the womb, O lord of men.
Having entered that very womb with his hundred-jointed thunderbolt, he [pierced it].
Then the wielder of the thunderbolt divided it again into seven parts, part by part.
He divided each one into seven parts, and then even the embryo began to cry out.
"Do not weep," said the wielder of the thunderbolt to him, remaining intent on his own task.
And at that very time, the mother of the lord of the Daityas then—
Having awakened, she restrained Śakra, the thousand-eyed one. || 15 ||
Śakra, with palms joined in the form of a vajra-garbha, was constrained by his mother’s words.
He emerged from her womb together with the high-souled children.
Diti spoke to Śakra, who stood before her with palms joined in reverence.
"O Śakra, there is no fault of yours in my cutting open the womb."
An enemy must always be restrained by every possible means by one who is skilled in policy.
"Due to my transgression, this embryo has been divided by you today into many parts. (18)
Let all the gods individually be known by the name Maruts.
"Since you, O Śakra, said to your sons, 'Do not weep' (mā rudadhvam)," ||19||
And thereafter, they shall be known as the Maruts throughout the three worlds.
They shall become your allies, remaining subject to your commands.
And no fear whatsoever shall ever arise from these for you.
Perform the division of their names and likewise their locations.
There is one light, two lights, and likewise three and four lights.
Ekaśakra, Dviśakra, Triśakra, and Mahābala; || 22 ||
In the first division of the wind, this group is known as Suratha.
Indraśca, Gavya, Dṛśya, and likewise Itaspratiśiras. || 23 ||
Mita, Sammita, and the mighty Amita.
In the second wind-sphere, there is a host named Praghoṣaṇa. ||24||
Ṛtajit and Satyajit, as well as Suṣeṇa and Senajit.
Atimitra, Amitra, Pṛrumitra, and Aparājita; || 25 ||
In the third wind-sphere, the host is known as Santāpana.
He is beyond the seasons, yet he possesses the seasons; he is the Ordainer, the Disposer, the Sustainer, and the Immutable.
The fourth, however, is known as the Gṛhamedha group, which consists of those who maintain their vows.
Such as this, similar to that, and like this, O consumer of nectar. || 27 ||
Krītana, Prasadṛkṣa, and the highly illustrious Sarabha.
And in the house is the one named Roṣaṇā, and in the fifth wind-sphere.
He is the sustainer, the one who crosses difficult paths, the fearless, the one who employs skillful means, the compassionate, and the patient.
In the sixth wind-element, however, the group known as Sāsvis is recorded. ||29||
Splendor, body, invisibility, desire, victory, and universal sovereignty.
The group named Prejeṣaṇa is in the seventh layer of wind.
Having assigned the division of names and their respective positions for these, Acyuta [spoke].
He went to his own home with joy, and Diti also went to her own home.
O hero among men, this supreme birth of the Maruts has been told to you, which removes the fear of sin.
In this world, let there be for people a livelihood through learning alone, and not through [the pursuit of] existence here.
Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-seventh chapter, titled "The Origin of the Maruts," in the first section of the Śrī Viṣṇudharmottara Purāṇa. 127.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
O Indra among kings, Danu gave birth to the foremost of the Dānavas.
The heroes headed by Vipracitti, who had taken refuge in the faction of the Daityas.
And she gave birth to Kāla, as well as the most dreadful Kālakeyas.
Those cruel ones who had taken refuge in the faction of the Daityas and were hostile toward the hosts of gods.
The son of Danāyu was the great asura named Vṛtra.
But Viruddha always sided with the faction of the Daityas, being opposed to the gods.
Siṃhikā gave birth to the great asuras known as the Saiṃhikeyas.
Many heroes of immeasurable splendor, headed by Rāhu and Śālva.
Learn from me of the divine Gandharvas, Apsarases, and Munis.
And Citrasena and Ugrasena, as well as Ūrṇāyu and Anagha. || 5 ||
Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gopa, and likewise Sūryavarcas.
Yugapastṛṇapa, Pārṣṇi, and likewise Ardhacitraratha. || 6 ||
Kali, Śāliśiras, Parjanya, and likewise Nārada.
And their younger sisters were beautiful, divine apsarases.
She is learned in the Vedas, irreproachable, the beloved leader of the hosts, and the sovereign of the Gaṇas.

Marīci, Śucikā, Vidyutparṇī, and Tilottamā.
Āṭṭikā, Lakṣmaṇā, Kṣemā, Devī, Rambhā, and Manoramā. || 9 ||
Āsitā, Subāhu, Suvratā, and likewise Suvapuḥ.
Puṇḍarīkā, Sugandhā, Sudārā, and likewise Surasā. || 1.128.10 ||
Hemā, Śaradvatī, and she who is Kamalā were also born [of her].

Among them, Viṣṇu, who assumes the form of a serpent, is the foremost and the remainder.
By which this earth, together with its mountains, forests, and groves, is supported.
Formerly, the form of Vāsudeva as Āheyī was described by me.
She is renowned as Anantā, the destroyer of the great kalpa.
In the great aeon, he always becomes himself a Great Being.
For Śeṣa, the upholder of the earth, was indeed born from a portion of him.

Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Ailāpatra, and Dhanañjaya.
Airāvata, Mahāpadma, and both Kambala and Aśvatara. || 16 ||
Śaṅkha, Padma, Mahāpadma, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and Balāhaka.
Nīlāśva, Puṣpadanta, Sumukha, and likewise Durmukha. || 17 ||
Nahuṣa, Kararoman, Kuru, and likewise Kulika.
